target_customer: Engineering and security teams at software companies (named customers include Cal.com, Guardant Health, b.well, Avora)
problem: Traditional static analysis produces many false positives and misses business logic and multi-step flaws, while pentests are one-time. Gecko models how an app should work, verifies exploits and proposes fixes.
business_model: B2B SaaS, AI-native SAST and code security platform sold to engineering and security teams

founders.name: Jeevan Jutla
founders.background_notes: Per YC page; top 500 globally in competitive hacking per YC page.

founders.name: Artemiy Malyshau
prior_employers: Interpol and national governments (threat intelligence software)
founders.background_notes: Per YC page. YC launch listings name only Jeevan Jutla as founder in some directories.

competitors.name: Semgrep
competitors.what: Pattern-matching static analysis tool, later adding AI-assisted features

technical_complexity.rationale: Building a compiler-accurate semantic model of codebases, finding multi-step logic flaws and verifying exploits is hard for two people; the founders have security research backgrounds and reported 30+ CVEs.

defensibility.rationale: Detection quality may differ, but large vendors and many AI SAST startups pursue the same approach, and results are hard for buyers to compare.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No acquisition found. Incumbents and AI code review tools added AI features through 2025 per comparison pages.

market_need_then: Static analysis tools are criticised for false positives and missed logic flaws, and AI coding increases code volume to review. No dated source near the batch was found; evidence is the founders' own launch claims.

branding.domain_note: Uses gecko.security, a TLD domain that spells the product category.

identity.visual_style: Olive-green and dark palette with dot patterns
identity.voice_and_tone: Direct; 'Get a Grip on Your Codebase' tagline plays on gecko grip

branding.brand_signature: Gecko mascot and the 'Get a Grip on Your Codebase' tagline
branding.community_and_virality: Launch HN thread and Product Hunt presence; a public dispute where FuzzingLabs accused Gecko of copying research (undated, unverified). No merch found.

brand_strength.rationale: A memorable animal mascot and a tagline that fits the product name; no evidence yet of growth driven by the brand.

outcome_analysis: Gecko Security is a two person London security startup from Fall 2024 YC that builds AI-native static analysis and claims 30+ CVEs found in open source projects. It lists recognizable customers and a seed round from YC and several funds, but the amount is not stated by the company. No exit or distress was found, and larger security vendors compete for the same wedge.
notes: Company blog (31 July 2025) confirms a seed round and lists investors but gives no amount or date. An aggregator reports 500K in December 2024; unverified. Competitor entry is from a July 2025 discussion, more than 18 months after founding is not true but the source postdates the batch by about 10 months, and traction is unknown. HQ conflict London (YC) versus San Francisco (aggregators). A FuzzingLabs allegation of copied research is undated and unverified.
